title: The Quadratic Formula: The Ultimate Weapon

blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: The Unbreakable Equation
blocks.content: A quadratic equation is any equation where the highest power of 'x' is 2, like **ax^2 + bx + c = 0**. When graphed, it creates a beautiful U-shaped curve called a parabola. Sometimes, these equations are easy to solve by factoring. But what happens when the numbers are ugly decimals or fractions? That's where the **Quadratic Formula** comes in. It is the ultimate weapon that can solve ANY quadratic equation in the universe.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: Memorizing the Magic
blocks.content:
To use the weapon, you must first memorize it:

**x = [-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / 2a**

• **a** is the number attached to x^2
• **b** is the number attached to x
• **c** is the lonely number at the end
• The **+/-** symbol means you will actually get TWO answers (one using +, one using -).

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: The Discriminant Trick
blocks.content:
The chunk of math sitting inside the square root, **(b^2 - 4ac)**, is incredibly special. It's called the **Discriminant**, and it acts like a crystal ball predicting the future of your graph:

1. Calculate (b^2 - 4ac) first before doing the whole formula.
2. If it's a **positive number**, the curve crosses the x-axis twice. You will have 2 real answers.
3. If it's **exactly zero**, the curve just kisses the x-axis once. You will have exactly 1 answer.
4. If it's a **negative number**, stop! You can't take the square root of a negative. There are 0 real answers.

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content:
Negative signs are the silent assassins of the Quadratic Formula. 
First, if 'b' is already negative (like -5), the formula asks for '-b', which flips it to a positive 5. Don't write -5! 
Second, when calculating b^2, remember that squaring a negative number ALWAYS makes it positive. (-5)^2 is +25, never -25. Keep your signs organized and you'll never fail.
